subject: Clarify 'Fee Shelter' trigger in Exhibit B & implementation steps
body:
From: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@clearskyhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@clearskyhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify fee shelter trigger in Exhibit B

Hi Olga —

Thanks again for the call earlier. Our procurement and legal teams asked us to get more precise language around the "fee shelter" / "stabilization" trigger in Exhibit B. Specifically: when does the shelter kick in (monthly threshold vs rolling 30-day), how true-ups are calculated (gross vs net of credits), and whether a temporary surcharge can be applied during a phased migration window.

Attached is a short doc with our suggested language (ExhibitB_FeeShelter_v1_redline.pdf). We tried to keep it narrow — mainly seeking: (1) a clear numeric trigger, (2) an implementation window and process, and (3) a short ops playbook so our billing and SRE teams know the steps.

Can your legal ops and pricing team review and confirm what Redwood can accept? We are trying to get an internal approval for an executive sign-off meeting next Friday.

Best,
Erin Walsh
Senior Procurement Manager
ClearSky Health

---

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@clearskyhealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify fee shelter trigger in Exhibit B

Erin —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. Quick summary from our side so we stay aligned:

- Trigger definition: Redwood prefers a calendar-month threshold (token-hours or committed compute units) rather than a rolling 30-day window for operational simplicity and consistent billing runs.
- True-up math: we calculate true-ups on billable tokens before external credits (i.e., gross billable usage) but we can show an itemized line for credits/offsets on the invoice.
- Temporary surcharge: acceptable during a short migration phase but needs a cap (we propose a 10% cap and a maximum period of 90 days).

I attached our markup to your ExhibitB draft. Main open items for us: whether ClearSky requires the shelter to be triggered on a per-region basis (would add complexity), and whether the surcharge must be waived if Redwood initiates capacity degradation.

Karthik, Laura — please see Erin's attachments and my inline comments. Can your teams produce a clean tracked-change draft we can circulate to Clearsky legal?

Action items:
- Karthik: draft operational definition for "monthly threshold" (hours vs tokens) and an ops checklist for activation/deactivation. Target: EOD Wed.
- Laura: confirm whether finance is okay with gross-true-up and produce sample invoice lines for transparency.
- Marissa: add a short paragraph to the order form describing the surcharge cap & rollback conditions.

Olga
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

---

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@clearskyhealth.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Mar 2027 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify fee shelter trigger in Exhibit B

Hi all —

Attaching the ops definition snippet (I pasted it into the shared Drive doc). Key calls:

- Measurement: the trigger will be measured on "billable token-hours" aggregated by calendar month in the billing region.
- Activation: once monthly usage exceeds the threshold for two consecutive months, the Fee Shelter enters test mode and the surcharge (if applicable) is batched for review.
- Deactivation: if usage falls below threshold for three consecutive months, shelter resets and any withheld credits are reconciled on the next invoice.

Notes:
- Per-region triggers add complexity to routing and KV cache accounting; recommend a single account-level threshold unless Clearsky requires region-level granularity.
- We propose a clear ops playbook that includes: notification (email + console alert), temporary rate cap (10%), manual review by SRE and billing ops, and a formal rollback window (30 days).

Let me know if this aligns with Clearsky's expectations and I will fold into the order form language.

Karthik
Director, Inference Operations (Redwood)

---

From: Tom Webster <t.webster@clearskyhealth.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@clearskyhealth.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 11:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify fee shelter trigger in Exhibit B

Olga / Karthik —

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A few legal points from ClearSky Legal on the proposed edits:

1) Trigger window: we can accept calendar-month measurement but need explicit fallbacks for billing disputes: (a) a 14-day clock to raise a dispute after invoice issuance, (b) a joint reconciliation audit clause once per year, and (c) explicit sample data exports (CSV schema) to aid our audit.

2) True-up basis: ClearSky asks that the language explicitly state whether third-party credits (e.g., marketplace credits or partner discounts) are excluded from the threshold calculation or only credited after the true-up calculation. We prefer credits excluded from threshold (i.e., threshold measured on net usage) — can Redwood live with that?

3) Surcharge & cap: we can agree to a temporary surcharge with a 10% cap but need two additions: (i) a pause-right if ClearSky submits a written escalation causing the surcharge to be reviewed, and (ii) an option to convert the surcharge into a credit if Redwood materially misses SLA targets during the surcharge window.

4) Ops playbook: we need a minimal timeline in the order form (e.g., Redwood to notify within 48 hours of trigger detection; billing ops to confirm within 10 business days).

If Redwood can accept the above edits I will provide a redlined version from our side and loop in procurement for final sign-off.

Tom Webster
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Procurement
ClearSky Health

---

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Tom Webster <t.webster@clearskyhealth.com>, Erin Walsh <erin.walsh@clearskyhealth.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Clarify fee shelter trigger in Exhibit B

Tom / Erin —

Appreciate the thoughtful notes. We can accept most of Clearsky's items with these confirmations:

- Disputes & audit: Redwood accepts the 14-day invoice dispute window and annual joint reconciliation audit. We will publish the CSV export schema and include a sample export clause in Exhibit B.
- Credits: Redwood can agree to measure the trigger on net billable usage (post third-party credits) provided ClearSky includes a consolidated credits schedule as an appendix so both teams are clear on what counts as a credit. We'll add explicit wording.
- Surcharge fail-safe: agree to the pause-right and SLA-conversion option. Need Laura to confirm the mechanics of converting surcharge to credit on invoice.
- Notification timelines: Redwood can commit to a 48-hour detection notification and a 10-business-day confirmation window. Ops checklist will be appended.

Next steps:
- Laura: provide precise invoice phrasing for surcharge conversion and a sample invoice line by EOD Fri so Clearsky can see the net effect.
- Marissa: I will incorporate the agreed language into OrderForm_CSH_Draft_20270316.docx and circulate for Tom's redline.
- Erin / Tom: once you confirm we will prepare an exec summary for sign-off next Friday.

Thanks — close to final.

Olga
Head of Enterprise Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: ExhibitB_FeeShelter_v1_redline.pdf (Clearsky initial), OrderForm_CSH_Draft_20270316.docx (Redwood draft with proposed language).

Related links: HubSpot deal RDW-2027-CSH-042, shared Drive folder with live redlines, DocuSign bridge for Order Form.
